name: Mastra Code

surfaces.label: Mastra Code TUI, launched through the npm bin shim (`mastracode`, `npx mastracode`, `bun add -g`, nvm or Homebrew node, or a project's node_modules/.bin). The bin is a `#!/usr/bin/env node` script, so ps shows `node <path>/bin/mastracode` with the SYMLINK path as argv[1] (inferred from shebang behaviour, never observed); npx and local installs give `.../node_modules/.bin/mastracode`, so the pattern is `bin/mastracode` without a leading slash. Nothing retitles the process (no process.title in the source or the 0.43.0 dist). `--prompt`, `-p`, `--acp`, `plugin`, `prune`, `--help` and `-h` are vetoed by exact argument. A bare positional prompt (`mastracode "fix it"`) also runs headless (hasHeadlessFlag) and is NOT vetoed here, so it reads as a TUI session; it is one-shot, alive means working.
Mastra Code TUI, node run on the real script (pnpm dlx, yarn dlx, a direct `node .../mastracode/dist/cli.js`, or a global install whose shim was resolved). Same vetoes as the shim surface.

Mastra Code headless one-shot: `mastracode --prompt "..."` (also `-o json|jsonl`, `--thread <id>`, `--continue`), through the bin shim. No TUI is built, so there is no caffeinate child. Alive means working. `-p` and a positional prompt cannot be matched separately (args_contain is a substring test and `-p` is too short); the `-p` form is vetoed on the TUI surfaces and is therefore invisible, the positional form shows as a TUI surface (see above). The launcher path is required as well as `--prompt`, so an unrelated node program whose prompt text mentions mastracode is not matched.

The launcher path is required as well as `--prompt`, so an unrelated node program whose prompt text mentions mastracode is not matched.

Mastra Code as an Agent Client Protocol server over stdio: `mastracode --acp [--dangerous-auto-approve]`, through the bin shim, spawned by an ACP client such as an editor. Runs many sessions in one process and has no TUI, so no caffeinate child. No per-session signal from outside. The launcher path is required as well as `--acp`.

working_signals.name: caffeinate
working_signals.meaning: The TUI spawns `caffeinate -i -m` (stdio ignored, direct child of the node process) on the controller's `agent_start` event and kills it on `agent_end` of any reason (complete, aborted, error, suspended). It is not there while idle. macOS only, and off when MASTRACODE_DISABLE_CAFFEINATE=1. TUI only: headless and ACP never start it. It stays through a tool-approval prompt (the approval is awaited inside the run) and drops for an ask_user, submit_plan or sandbox-access suspension (those end the run as `suspended`).

Shell commands from the built-in execute_command tool run through the default LocalSandbox with isolation 'none', which spawns with `shell: true` and `detached: true`, so each is a direct `/bin/sh -c <command>` child. Caveat: a lone simple command may be exec'd in place by sh, so the direct child is then the command, not a shell. MCP servers and LSP servers also live as direct children but are not shells. Caveat 2: user hook commands are ALSO direct `/bin/sh -c` children of the TUI (hooks/executor.ts), short-lived (10 s default timeout). Stop, AgentEnd and Notification hooks (agent_done) run after the run has ended, so with hooks configured an idle TUI can show a shell child for a moment right after a turn. Apply the 5 s debounce and let the caffeinate child decide.
Guess, not measured. Fallback only: the TUI redraws a status timer while a run is active.

waiting_signals.meaning: Fires as soon as the TUI receives a prompt event, before the TUI's own queue. Payload carries permission_kind: tool_approval, sandbox_access or plan_approval, plus run_id, tool_name and tool_input. Closed by PermissionResult (approve, decline or dismiss) with the same run_id. Needs ~/.mastracode/hooks.json.

The TUI's notify() also fires Notification hooks with reason tool_approval, ask_question, plan_approval, sandbox_access (waiting on the human) or agent_done (run finished, waiting for input). Fires even when the built-in bell/system notification mode is off.
stop_reason `suspended` means the run parked on an ask_user, submit_plan or sandbox-access question. `complete`, `aborted` and `error` mean idle.

Process side, inferred from source: a live TUI with no caffeinate child is idle OR parked on an ask_user, plan or sandbox-access question; the two cannot be told apart without a hook. A tool-approval wait still shows caffeinate, so it reads as working.

hooks.config: ~/.mastracode/hooks.json (global, runs first) and .mastracode/hooks.json (project, appended after); `/hooks reload` re-reads. Disabled by MASTRACODE_DISABLE_HOOKS=1. Command hooks get a JSON payload on stdin with session_id (the thread id), cwd, hook_event_name and, during a run, run_id.

telemetry.how: No OTLP exporter in mastracode. Its Mastra Observability config (serviceName mastracode) has two exporters: MastraStorageExporter into a local DuckDB file (opt-in with `/observability local on`, ~/Library/Application Support/mastracode/observability.duckdb) and MastraPlatformExporter to Mastra's cloud. Separate PostHog product analytics, opt out with MASTRA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. Nothing to point a local collector at.

notes: Matching reads the command line only, and Mastra Code is a plain node script, so the row has to match on the script path and cannot use a process name. Never key on `node` alone. The working signal is the direct `caffeinate -i -m` child, which exists only while a run is active (macOS, TUI only). It is the most precise signal and is not paired with a wait record: a tool-approval wait keeps caffeinate (reads as working), an ask_user, plan or sandbox-access wait drops it (reads as idle); hooks (PermissionRequest, Notification, AgentEnd suspended) are the only exact wait signal. Sessions are threads in one shared SQLite file, so there is no per-session transcript file and no per_session path; map a process to a thread through a hook session_id, `--thread` on a headless run, or (inferred, unverified) the /tmp/mc/<resourceId>/<threadId>.sock listeners shown by lsof -U. Never read message columns. Do not count the osascript notification helper as a tool child. User hook commands are direct `/bin/sh -c` children too (short-lived, also right after a turn ends), so debounce the shell signal. If stdin is piped and no TTY can be reopened, the TUI command falls back to headless (main.ts ~424) and shows as a TUI surface here. Nothing here has been run: no Mastra Code was installed or running on this Mac.
